source_text:
Ἀπάτωρ
γὰρ ἐπὶ γῆς Χριστὸς κατὰ σάρκα, ἀμήτωρ ἐν οὐρανοῖς κατὰ πνεῦμα κατὰ τὴν θεότητα· τοιοῦτόν ἐστι καὶ τὸ μήτε ἀρχὴν ἡμερῶν μήτε ζωῆς τέλος ἔχων. Οὐ γὰρ ἐγενεαλόγησεν ἡ γραφὴ τὸν Μελχισεδέκ, ἀλλὰ παρέλιπεν αὐτοῦ τὴν γέννησιν καὶ τὴν τελευτήν, ἵνα, καθὰ προείπαμεν, ἐν ἐκείνῳ τοῦτον θεωρήσωμεν. Βασιλεὺς γὰρ δικαιοσύνης ἑρμηνεύεται Μελχισεδέκ, ὅς ἐστι Χριστὸς μήτε ἀρχὴν ἡμερῶν ἕχων μήτε ζωῆς τέλος· οὔτε γὰρ ἐν ἀρχῇ ἡμερῶν ὁ Θεὸς Λόγος ἐγεννήθη, οὔτε ἔληξέ ποτε ἢ ἐτελεύτησεν, εἰς ἀεὶ γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς διαμένει. Οὕτως οὖν ὁ Μελχισεδὲκ ἀνὴρ δίκαιος γέγονε καὶ ἀληθῶς εἰκόνα Θεοῦ φέρων ἐν ἑαυτῷ· προφητικῷ τοίνυν πνεύματι κινούμενος τὴν μέλλουσαν ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ προσφορὰν τῷ Θεῷ προσκομίζεσθαι νοήσας, ἄρτῳ καὶ οἴνῳ τὸν Θεὸν ἐγέραιρεν μιμούμενος τὸν μέλλοντα Χριστόν. Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίων συναγωγῇ ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἀαρὼν θυσίαν προσέφερε τῷ Θεῷ, οὐκ ἄρτον καὶ οἶνον, ἀλλὰ μόσχους καὶ ἀμνούς, ἐναίμοις θυσίαις δοξάζουσα τὸν Θεόν, ὁ Θεὸς πρὸς τὸν μέλλοντα γεννᾶσθαι ἐκ τῆς παρθένου Μαρίας Ἰησοῦν ἐβόα λέγων· Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ, οὐ κατὰ τὸν Ἀαρὼν τὸν ἐναίμοις θυσίαις λατρεύοντα, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδὲκ ἐν ἄρτῳ καὶ οἴνῳ τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν προσκομίζων προσφορὰν εἰς τὸ διηνεκές.
thought_title: Christ the true Melchizedek: without father on earth, without mother in heaven
orientation: Eustathius is closing his treatise by explaining how Melchizedek's unrecorded genealogy points to Christ, who alone is truly without father on earth and without mother in heaven.
pass_a_gloss: For without father on earth [is] Christ according to flesh, without mother in heavens according to spirit according to the divinity; such [a thing] is also the [one] having neither beginning of days nor end of life. For the Scripture did not trace a genealogy [for] Melchizedek, but omitted his birth and his death, in order that, just as we said before, in that one we might behold this one. For king of righteousness is interpreted Melchizedek, who is Christ having neither beginning of days nor end of life; for neither in beginning of days was God the Word begotten, nor did he ever cease or die, for forever Christ remains. Thus therefore Melchizedek was a righteous man and truly bearing [the] image of God in himself; moved therefore by prophetic spirit, having understood the offering about to be brought to God by Christ, with bread and wine he was honoring God, imitating the Christ who was to come. Since therefore in the synagogue of the Jews the order of Aaron was offering sacrifice to God, not bread and wine, but calves and lambs, glorifying God with bloody sacrifices, God toward the Jesus about to be born from the virgin Mary cried out saying: You [are] priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek, not according to Aaron the [one] serving with bloody sacrifices, but according to the order of Melchizedek, in bread and wine bringing the offering of the nations perpetually.

choices.term: Ἀπάτωρ γὰρ ἐπὶ γῆς Χριστὸς κατὰ σάρκα
choices.english: For Christ is without father on earth according to the flesh
choices.why: Keeps the predicate adjective first as in Greek, preserving the emphasis on 'without father' as the opening claim
rejected: For Christ on earth is fatherless according to the flesh

choices.term: ἀμήτωρ ἐν οὐρανοῖς κατὰ πνεῦμα κατὰ τὴν θεότητα
choices.english: without mother in the heavens according to the spirit, according to the divinity
choices.why: Renders both κατὰ phrases literally to preserve the double qualification of Christ's heavenly existence
rejected: motherless in heaven in spirit and divinity

choices.term: μήτε ἀρχὴν ἡμερῶν μήτε ζωῆς τέλος ἔχων
choices.english: having neither beginning of days nor end of life
choices.why: Keeps the exact negation pair and the participle construction, matching the Hebrews 7:3 allusion
rejected: with no beginning of days or end of life

choices.why: Preserves the dative of instrument and the inferential τοίνυν, showing Melchizedek's action was Spirit-driven
Uses the glossary term 'bloody sacrifice' in the plural dative, matching the contrast with bread and wine

choices.term: τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν προσκομίζων προσφορὰν εἰς τὸ διηνεκές
choices.english: bringing the offering of the nations perpetually
choices.why: Keeps the participle and the phrase 'of the nations' as the object of the offering, preserving the universal scope
rejected: offering the offering of the Gentiles forever

Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ

pass_b_english: For Christ is without father on earth according to the flesh, and without mother in the heavens according to the spirit, according to the divinity. Such also is the one who has neither beginning of days nor end of life. Scripture did not trace a genealogy for Melchizedek, but omitted his birth and his death, so that, as we said before, we might behold this one in him. For Melchizedek is interpreted as king of righteousness, who is Christ, having neither beginning of days nor end of life. The Word of God was neither begotten at a beginning of days, nor did he ever cease or come to an end, for Christ remains forever.

So Melchizedek was a righteous man and truly bore the image of God in himself. Moved therefore by prophetic spirit, he understood the offering that was to be brought to God by Christ, and he honored God with bread and wine, imitating the Christ who was to come. Since in the synagogue of the Jews the order of Aaron offered sacrifice to God—not bread and wine, but calves and lambs, glorifying God with bloody sacrifices—God cried out to Jesus, who was to be born from the virgin Mary, saying: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek (Psalm 109:4), not according to Aaron, who served with bloody sacrifices, but according to the order of Melchizedek, bringing the offering of the nations in bread and wine perpetually.

problems.source_quote: Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ
problems.why: Source uses Septuagint Psalm 109, not Psalm 110.

edits.old: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek (Psalm 110:4)
edits.new: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek (Psalm 109:4)

problems.why: Same concept rendered in four different orders; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Standardize or note order is rhetorical.

variants.text: without father, without mother, and without genealogy
without father on earth according to the flesh, and without mother in the heavens

problems.quote: king of Salem—that is, of this much-talked-of Jerusalem
problems.why: Two different translations/explanations of Melchizedek's name/title; reader may think they are separate concepts.
problems.fix: Note both are traditional interpretations of the name.

variants.text: king of Salem—that is, of this much-talked-of Jerusalem

problems.quote: God cried out to Jesus, who was to be born from the virgin Mary
problems.why: 'Cried out' suggests prophetic oracle but sounds abrupt; may misrepresent Hebrews' citation formula.

problems.quote: bringing the offering of the nations in bread and wine perpetually
problems.why: Subject is unclear: God? Christ? The order? 'Bringing' seems to dangle.
problems.fix: Clarify subject: Christ brings this offering.

edits.old: God cried out to Jesus, who was to be born from the virgin Mary, saying:
edits.new: God declared to Jesus, who was to be born from the virgin Mary, saying:

edits.old: but according to the order of Melchizedek, bringing the offering of the nations in bread and wine perpetually.
edits.new: but according to the order of Melchizedek, in bread and wine bringing the offering of the nations perpetually.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'without mother and without father' is not a problem in this section: the English renders the source order exactly (without father... without mother), and the source itself uses that order.
The glossary issue about 'king of Salem—that is, of this much-talked-of Jerusalem' does not appear in this section; the English only has 'king of righteousness,' which matches the source.
Changed 'cried out' to 'declared' to avoid the abrupt prophetic-oracle tone.

Clarified the dangling participle by restoring the source's word order: 'in bread and wine bringing the offering of the nations perpetually,' which ties the action to the order of Melchizedek as in the source.

last_rejected.quote: God cried out to Jesus, who was to be born from the virgin Mary, saying: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek (Psalm 109:4)
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ Θεὸς πρὸς τὸν μέλλοντα γεννᾶσθαι ἐκ τῆς παρθένου Μαρίας Ἰησοῦν ἐβόα λέγων· Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ
last_rejected.why: Speaker attribution to God is clear in English; matches source marking.
last_rejected.ruling: No error reported; English correctly renders ὁ Θεὸς...ἐβόα as 'God cried out.'

last_rejected.source_quote: Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ
last_rejected.why: Brief states Psalm 109 in LXX corresponds to Psalm 110 in Hebrew numbering; citation should specify LXX numbering or use Hebrew 110.
last_rejected.ruling: Psalm 109:4 is valid LXX numbering; not a wrong reference, just different numbering system.

last_rejected.quote: bringing the offering of the nations in bread and wine perpetually
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐν ἄρτῳ καὶ οἴνῳ τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν προσκομίζων προσφορὰν εἰς τὸ διηνεκές
last_rejected.why: English makes 'bringing' a participle without clear subject; Christ is subject of the whole clause, but 'bringing' could misread as Aaron or God. The Greek has Christ as the one who brings the offering.
last_rejected.fix: he brings the offering of the nations in bread and wine perpetually
last_rejected.ruling: Greek προσκομίζων participle also lacks explicit subject; English mirrors source syntax faithfully.
